proposed.explanation: Publication prestige does not fulfill the Code's specific requirement for professional consensus and academic/experience backing. [cite: 98] External recognition is valuable, but the Code requires specialization claims to be substantiated facts sanctioned by the profession. [cite: 98] The prohibition is on exaggerated or misleading publicity; the lack of payment doesn't make an unsubstantiated specialization claim valid. [cite: 98, 126] Specialization claims require professional consensus and substantiated years of experience; individual media recognition is not equivalent to professional consensus. [cite: 90, 98] Misrepresenting qualifications by claiming specialization without substantiated professional consensus is an ethical violation. [cite: 90, 94, 98]
